hypothesis: The vector FPU decodes the FMA array's controls (operand form, negate, multiply-only, reduction override) from the X-stage opcode, and that decode drives ~1500 operand-mux bits across sixteen lanes in front of the FMA's first stage. Decoding it in R from the same opcode and registering it with the opcode removes the decode and most of the fan-out tree without moving a cycle.
evidence_for_hypothesis: tnca_fpga_top post-synthesis, 6.667 ns target, after timing-003: x_func -> u_vfpu/g_fma[12].u_fma p0_res_sign_mag 7.167 ns / 28 levels, 2.3 ns of it before the multiplier's B input (x_func fan-out 185 into the operand muxes)

microarch.change: tnca_vector_fpu takes fpctl[4:0] = {is FP reduction, vf.mul, vf.sub|vf.fms, func==MUL, func==ADD|SUB}, decoded by the core from r_major/r_func and loaded into x_fpctl in the same R->X transfer as x_major/x_func; the unit's own case on major/func for the FMA operands is gone

compatibility.cycles: unchanged: R2 cycle check over the 149 R37 O2 cases, and every core program
compatibility.numerics: identical by construction: fpctl is the same function of the same opcode one register earlier; unit fp32 benches and every core program

resource.kind: Vivado 2023.2 post-synthesis, out of context, xcu280-fsvh2892-2L-e, 6.667 ns target

change.worst_path: x_fpctl[4] -> operand mux -> 24x24 multiplier -> alignment compare; the rest is inside the generated FMA's first stage
